title: Program–Matrix–Interface Co-Design for Calibrated Cyanobacterial Living Photovoltaic Materials
topic: How can matter be programmed into engineered living materials through synthetic biology, genomic engineering, and living–nonliving self-assembly?

source.evidence_use: The cited Survey anchors support problem framing and feasibility of the component classes. They do not establish that the proposed combined co-design mechanism already works.

directions.title: Program–Matrix–Interface Co-Design for Calibrated Cyanobacterial Living Photovoltaic Materials
directions.abstract: Engineered living materials often demonstrate a programmable cellular component, a material scaffold, or an improved bioelectronic interface separately, but lack a causal map that links cellular state to interfacial architecture and device-level function. This idea proposes a bounded cyanobacterial living-photovoltaic research program in which a programmable extracellular-matrix and attachment state is considered jointly with a biocompatible conductive interface. The claim is not that either element alone increases output; it is that their combination can create a continuous, durable biological-to-abiotic electron-extraction path. The key test is an interaction: after normalizing for viable biomass, illuminated area, and contact geometry, the combined condition should improve photoelectrical output and charge-transfer behavior beyond either single-factor condition, while retaining photosynthetic activity over repeated illumination cycles. A state-to-function map, rather than a one-off performance maximum, is the intended contribution.

hypothesis.central_hypothesis: Within a cyanobacterial living-photovoltaic composite, coupling a cellular program that regulates extracellular-matrix and attachment state with a biocompatible conductive interface will yield a persistent increase in biomass-normalized photoelectrical output and a lower interfacial charge-transfer resistance than either intervention alone, because the biological state and abiotic interface jointly establish a continuous electron-extraction path.

scientific_object.biological_component: programmable photosynthetic cyanobacterial population with an extracellular-matrix and attachment phenotype
scientific_object.material_component: biocompatible conductive, optically compatible cell-contact interface coupled to a current collector
scientific_object.target_relation: cellular program and matrix/attachment state -> interface architecture -> extracellular electron extraction -> stable normalized photoelectrical function

hypothesis.mechanism_or_relation: A matrix/attachment phenotype changes cell–interface contact organization and local transport paths; a conductive, biocompatible interface provides the complementary abiotic extraction path. Their joint state is predicted to lower interfacial transport limitation without treating larger biomass alone as the mechanism.
hypothesis.intervention_or_transformation: At the level of research design, contrast a baseline living photovoltaic composite with biological-program-only, material-interface-only, and combined program–matrix–interface conditions. The Idea stage specifies no construct sequence, strain engineering procedure, culture condition, electrode fabrication recipe, or operational protocol.
hypothesis.expected_mechanism: Only the combined condition should produce a reproducible interaction in normalized photoelectrical output, charge-transfer proxy, and temporal stability that remains after accounting for viable biomass, optical exposure, and effective contact area.
hypothesis.discriminating_observation: The combined condition exceeds the additive or single-factor improvement in viable-biomass-normalized photocurrent and shows a concordant reduction in interfacial charge-transfer proxy while its matrix/contact architecture and photosynthetic-activity proxy remain consistent with the proposed path.
hypothesis.evidence_requirement: Demonstrate the direction and persistence of the combined-versus-single-factor contrast; report viable biomass, illuminated area, interface/contact architecture, charge-transfer proxy, photosynthetic activity, and repeated-cycle stability so that attachment, optical, and geometry confounders can be separated from the mechanism.
evidence_basis: The Survey identifies programmable extracellular matrices and microbial inks as routes from cell state to material architecture (R4–R6).
The Survey identifies both biological electron export and the cell–electrode interface as constraints in living photovoltaics (R9–R13).
The proposed interaction and calibration map are new hypotheses; no source anchor is treated as direct evidence for their combined causal effect.
hypothesis.boundary_or_failure_condition: The claim fails or is narrowed if the apparent benefit disappears after normalization for viable biomass/contact area, compromises photosynthetic activity or optical access, does not persist across repeated illumination cycles, or cannot be separated from coating-only adhesion and geometry effects.
hypothesis.claim_scope: Cyanobacterial living-photovoltaic composites operated within the explicitly documented viable, illuminated, and optically compatible regime; the Idea makes no claim about all organisms, all electrode materials, clinical use, industrial scale-up, or autonomous self-repair.
assumptions: A measurable matrix/attachment state can be represented without reducing the research question to total cell number.
The selected conductive interface can be evaluated while preserving a viable, photosynthetically active cell population.
Normalized output, interfacial transport proxy, architecture, and time-dependent stability can be measured in comparable units across conditions.
The combined condition can be compared with matched single-factor controls without changing the core optical geometry.

gap_alignment.statement: The Survey identifies no general predictive mapping from genetic program through cell state and matrix/interface architecture to material property.
Living-photovoltaic work documents biological and interface constraints, but does not resolve whether their joint optimization has a mechanism distinct from adhesion, biomass, or geometry.
Cross-study comparison is limited by inconsistent viability, interface, and functional metrology; a normalized state-to-function map is needed.

trace.scientific_concern: An apparent output gain can arise from higher retained biomass, altered optical scattering, or changed electrode geometry rather than a coupled program–matrix–interface mechanism.
trace.required_revision: Require matched single-factor conditions and normalize photoelectrical readouts to viable biomass, illuminated area, and effective contact architecture.
alternative_explanations: The interface material merely increases retained viable biomass.
The apparent gain is caused by altered light scattering, transparency, or electrode geometry.
Growth phase or metabolic state, rather than the programmed matrix/interface coupling, changes the output.
A non-specific coating effect changes adhesion without improving electron extraction.
trace.final_scope: A bounded, comparative claim about a cyanobacterial living-photovoltaic composite; not a universal material-programming claim.

experiment_handoff.claim_to_test: Within a cyanobacterial living-photovoltaic composite, coupling a cellular program that regulates extracellular-matrix and attachment state with a biocompatible conductive interface will yield a persistent increase in biomass-normalized photoelectrical output and a lower interfacial charge-transfer resistance than either intervention alone, because the biological state and abiotic interface jointly establish a continuous electron-extraction path.

gap_records.statement: No predictive program -> cell-state -> matrix/interface architecture -> material-property map is established for the stated system.
gap_records.why_it_matters: Without the map, genetic and material changes cannot be distinguished from empirical optimization.

gap_records.statement: Biological electron-export capacity and the cell–electrode interface are both constraints, but their causal interaction is unresolved.
gap_records.why_it_matters: A joint mechanism must be distinguished from biomass, adhesion, and optical artefacts.

gap_records.statement: Current ELM studies lack a standardized comparator set spanning viability, architecture, transport, function, and persistence.
gap_records.why_it_matters: A normalized, time-resolved state-to-function record makes the result comparable and falsifiable.

scientific_object.description: Programmable photosynthetic cells, a matrix/attachment phenotype, a conductive biocompatible interface, and a transparent current-collection architecture considered as one coupled material system.

experiment_handoff.mechanism_to_discriminate: Joint biological matrix/attachment organization and abiotic conductive transport improve extracellular electron extraction beyond the independent contribution of either factor.
experiment_handoff.claim_scope: Only the stated cyanobacterial living-photovoltaic composite and its documented viable, illuminated, optically compatible operating regime.
assumptions: Single-factor and combined conditions can be compared without changing the underlying optical geometry.
Viability, photosynthetic activity, matrix/contact architecture, and interfacial transport can be observed as separate outcome classes.
The proposed material interface is evaluated for biological compatibility rather than presumed inert.
boundary_conditions: Benefits disappear after normalization for viable biomass or contact area.
The intervention reduces photosynthetic activity, cell viability, or optical transparency below the viable functional regime.
The output improvement does not persist across repeated illumination cycles.
Batch-to-batch variability prevents a reproducible state-to-function relationship.
alternative_explanations: Increased retained biomass alone accounts for the signal.
Illumination, scattering, transparency, or collector geometry accounts for the signal.
Metabolic state or growth phase accounts for the signal.
A coating-only adhesion effect accounts for the signal without improving electron extraction.
required_observations: Photoelectrical output normalized to viable biomass and illuminated area, evaluated over time rather than at one endpoint.
An interfacial charge-transfer or impedance proxy measured with comparable geometry across conditions.
A viability and photosynthetic-activity proxy recorded alongside electrical function.
A measurement of matrix/contact architecture sufficient to distinguish contact organization from total biomass.
The combined-versus-single-factor interaction after accounting for biomass, optical exposure, and contact area.

evidence_roles.expected_role: Defines engineered living materials as biological systems that direct smart-material assembly.
evidence_roles.claim_limits: Background only; it does not establish the proposed bioelectronic co-design mechanism.

evidence_roles.expected_role: Supports the feasibility of genetically programmed extracellular material architecture.
evidence_roles.claim_limits: Does not test cyanobacterial photoelectrical extraction or this combined interface hypothesis.

evidence_roles.expected_role: Identifies synthetic biology as a route to engineering living photovoltaics.
evidence_roles.claim_limits: Does not demonstrate a matrix/interface interaction.

evidence_roles.expected_role: Shows that live cyanobacteria can generate photocurrent in a living photovoltaic context.
evidence_roles.claim_limits: It does not establish that programmed attachment and a conductive interface act synergistically.

evidence_roles.expected_role: Motivates the cell–interface as a modifiable electron-transfer bottleneck.
evidence_roles.claim_limits: A coating-related improvement can still be explained by adhesion, biomass, or non-specific interface effects.

evidence_roles.expected_role: Motivates conductive three-dimensional interfaces as a route to improved biophotovoltaic performance.
evidence_roles.claim_limits: It does not supply the biological-program arm or prove a general program-to-property map.

risks: The biological program and conductive interface may be incompatible, resulting in lower viability or photosynthetic activity.
The interaction may be too small relative to batch, geometry, or illumination variability.
An increased output may remain inseparable from adhesion or optical artefacts without architecture-aware normalization.
A material optimized for conductivity may reduce optical compatibility or long-term biological function.
known_unknowns: Which matrix/attachment state is both programmable and informative for electron extraction in the selected cyanobacterial chassis.
Which interface characteristics preserve viability while providing a measurable transport benefit.
Whether the interaction is durable under repeated operation rather than transiently favorable.
Whether a transferable program–architecture–function map can be obtained across batches or only for one material system.

directions.mature_idea: A bounded, causal idea that turns the broad question of programming matter into a testable program–matrix–interface interaction in cyanobacterial living photovoltaics.

source_lineage.contribution: ELM program-to-material framing, living photovoltaic interface bottleneck, and evidence limitations.

directions.independence_rationale: The idea combines a cellular state-to-architecture map with an interface-transport discrimination requirement; the supplied Survey anchors motivate its components but do not report this combined causal design.

legacy_best_entry.title: Program–Matrix–Interface Co-Design for Calibrated Cyanobacterial Living Photovoltaic Materials
legacy_best_entry.abstract: A bounded research idea that tests whether a programmed matrix/attachment state and a biocompatible conductive interface jointly improve persistent, normalized living-photovoltaic function.
legacy_best_entry.central_hypothesis: Within a cyanobacterial living-photovoltaic composite, coupling a cellular program that regulates extracellular-matrix and attachment state with a biocompatible conductive interface will yield a persistent increase in biomass-normalized photoelectrical output and a lower interfacial charge-transfer resistance than either intervention alone.

scientific_object.target_relation: cellular program -> matrix/interface architecture -> electron extraction -> stable photoelectrical function

legacy_best_entry.mechanism_or_relation: Joint biological attachment/matrix organization and conductive interface transport provide a continuous electron-extraction path.
legacy_best_entry.intervention_or_transformation: Compare conceptual baseline, biological-program-only, material-interface-only, and combined conditions without specifying operational procedures at the Idea stage.
legacy_best_entry.discriminating_observation: A combined-versus-single-factor interaction remains after viable-biomass, illuminated-area, and contact-architecture normalization.
legacy_best_entry.evidence_requirement: Joint electrical, transport, viability, photosynthetic-activity, architecture, and repeated-cycle observations.
legacy_best_entry.boundary_or_failure_condition: Loss of normalized benefit, viability, optical compatibility, persistence, or reproducibility invalidates or narrows the claim.
assumptions: The interface remains biologically compatible and optically suitable.
The matrix/attachment phenotype is separable from biomass alone.
Matched single-factor comparators can be maintained.
legacy_best_entry.falsifier: The combined condition has no positive interaction in normalized photoelectrical and transport readouts, or its apparent gain is fully explained by biomass, adhesion, optical exposure, or geometry.
known_unknowns: The transferable form of the program–architecture–function map remains unknown.
Long-term compatibility of the biological and conductive components remains unknown.
